title: Android Board Widget
eyebrow: Plan for approval · Android only · nothing built yet

short.lead: You asked for a widget on your Android home screen that shows one project's Board, where you can tick tasks off and move them between columns without opening the app. That project is a local list, not one linked to GitHub. Today Focus Deck is a web app installed from Chrome, and Chrome gives web apps no way to put a widget on the home screen (the Chrome request is still open: issues.chromium.org/issues/40744630). So the plan wraps the same Focus Deck code in a small Android app, built with Capacitor (free and open source), and adds a native widget to it. The pictures are drawings of the plan, not the built widget.
short.hint: Tap each circle to see its picture.
items: You install Focus Deck from Chrome. All your tasks live in Chrome's storage for the site, which only Chrome can open. Nothing outside Chrome, a widget included, can read or change them. Chrome's own Android wrapper (a Trusted Web Activity) keeps the data in Chrome too, so it can't help either.

The widget shows the same three tabs as the Board: Up next, In progress and Done this week, with their counts, for the project you picked. Each task has a box to tick it off and a button that moves it one column, the same '→ In progress' and '← Up next' buttons the Board already has. The list scrolls. 'Open' starts the app on that project's Board. Android widgets can't drag, so moving is by button.

items.alt: A phone home screen with a Focus Deck widget for the Home project showing three Up next tasks, each with a tick box and a move to In progress button
items.caption: The widget on the Up next tab.

items: Ticking a task marks it done straight away and saves it. The ticked task stays in place for a few seconds, crossed out, with an Undo button, then moves into Done. The change is saved the same way a change in the app is, so the app shows it next time it opens.
Look at the crossed-out task and its Undo button.

items.alt: The widget on the In progress tab, with Renew the car tax ticked, crossed out and showing an Undo button
items.caption: Just after ticking 'Renew the car tax'.

items: When you add the widget, Android shows a short list of your projects to pick from. You can add several widgets, one per project, and long-press one later to change its project.

items.alt: A full-screen list asking which project the widget should show: Home, Work admin, Garden and All projects
items.caption: Choosing the project when adding the widget.

items: The Android app is built automatically on GitHub and attached to the repo's Releases page as an APK, the file Android installs apps from. You download it on your phone once and allow your browser to install apps. No Play Store account is needed. Your tasks move over once, as chosen below.
Choose how your tasks move over, and how app updates arrive.

changes: chg
New Android app
The same Focus Deck code, wrapped with Capacitor, plus the widget.
The repo gains an android folder. The widget code is written in Kotlin, Android's own language, using Jetpack Glance, Google's toolkit for widgets.
chg
Where your tasks are saved, inside the Android app
The app also writes them where the widget can reach them.

Inside the Android app, every save is copied to the phone's app storage (Android's SharedPreferences). Changes made in the widget are stamped and merged back by the app's existing merge code, the same code that already merges Gist sync copies, so two edits never overwrite each other silently.
chg
GitHub build
Builds the APK and attaches it to a Release.
The signing key, which proves updates come from you, is kept as a GitHub secret, never in the repo. I'll generate it; losing it means future updates can't install over the old app.
keep
The web app and the Chrome install
No change.
GitHub Pages keeps serving the web app, and any computer or phone can still install it from Chrome. The widget exists only in the Android app.
keep
Board rules
No change.
The widget uses the same columns, the same order and the same move rules as the Board.
choices: How should your current tasks get into the new Android app?
Settings gets 'Save a copy' and 'Load a copy'. You save from the Chrome app and load in the new one. It works offline and doesn't need GitHub sync.
If your phone already syncs to a Gist, you sign in once in the new app and everything arrives. Nothing new is built, but it only works if sync is on.
I suggest A because it works whether or not sync is on, and the copy file is also a handy backup.
How should app updates reach the Android app?
Load the app from GitHub Pages

The Android app opens the live web app, so every change you merge arrives by itself, as it does now. Only widget changes need a new APK. It still works offline after the first open. Capacitor's documentation describes live loading as a development feature, so I'd test it carefully.
Pack the app inside the APK
This is the standard Capacitor setup and the safest. Every change, however small, means downloading and installing a new APK.
I suggest A because it keeps updates arriving the way they do today.

wrapup.summary: A live, tickable Board widget is only possible inside an Android app, so the plan wraps Focus Deck in one and adds the widget. The web app and the Chrome install stay as they are.
wrapup.changing: Added: an Android app, its widget, and a GitHub build that publishes the APK. Kept: the web app, GitHub Pages, and the Board's rules.
wrapup.blocking: I am waiting for your answers to the two questions in Choices. Nothing is built until you approve.
wrapup.next: After you approve, I open a parent issue with one child issue per step, then build on a new branch. I can build and run the tests here, but I can't run an Android phone, so the last check is you installing the APK and trying the widget.
